short: An annual payment to eligible employees, minimum set by law.
seoTitle: Statutory Bonus — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: An annual payment to eligible employees, minimum set by law. Many businesses pay it around the festive season. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Statutory bonus is an annual payment to eligible employees under the Payment of Bonus Act, subject to a minimum percentage of wages and a wage eligibility ceiling. Many businesses pay it around the festive season.
bodyHtml:
Why Statutory Bonus matters

Bonus is a legal obligation for covered establishments rather than a discretionary gift, and it is often paid on top of whatever informal festive payments a business already makes.

How Statutory Bonus works in practice

Budget for it through the year rather than absorbing it in one month, and keep the statutory bonus distinct from discretionary incentives in both records and communication.

faq.question: Who is eligible for statutory bonus?
faq.answer: Employees earning up to the prescribed wage ceiling who have worked the minimum number of days in the year.

faq.question: Is a performance incentive the same as statutory bonus?
faq.answer: No. Performance pay is contractual or discretionary; statutory bonus is a legal minimum for covered employees.
